body:
Does this section cover newer techniques such as GraphQL?  I think it should as the introduction mentions being forward thinking

"Ensure that a verified application that uses RESTful or SOAP based web services has" -> "Ensure that a verified application that uses a server-side API (commonly using JSON or XML or GraphQL) has"

In the Control Objective, you might want to mention that previous requirements apply to APIs as well (access control, security in transit, etc.)

Add a link to:

REST Security Cheat Sheet
https://www.owasp.org/index.php/REST_Security_Cheat_Sheet

Additions:

Add that authorization decisions should be at both the URI and resource level, not just at the resource level

For GraphQL:

If GraphQL is used, to prevent DoS as a result of expensive, nested queries, query whitelisting or a combination of depth limiting and amount limiting should be used.  For more advanced scenarios, query cost analysis should be used

If GraphQL is used, authorization logic should be implemented at the business logic layer instead of the GraphQL layer

comments.body: This is a good suggestion. Probably need to think about web sockets and other mechanisms as well.
